title: 🏛️ Exams 2023–2026 · the simple past: regular and irregular ⭐⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026) Complete the sentence with the correct form: "Noah and her family spent their last spring holidays in France. Before getting back home, they ___ nice souvenirs for their friends."
questions.explanation: The holidays are over ("spent their last spring holidays"), so the verb goes into the simple past, and choose is irregular: its past form is chose. The bare form is the present, the form with will is the future, and the form ending in -ed adds the regular ending to a verb that refuses it.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) Complete the sentence with the correct form: "Last week, the pupils organised a party for Teachers' Day. Students ___ nice songs and gave special cards to their teachers."
questions.explanation: "Last week" is a finished moment, so the verb goes into the simple past, and sing is irregular: its past form is sang. The bare form is the present, the form with will is the future, and the form ending in -ed adds the regular ending to a verb that has a past of its own.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025) Complete the sentence with the word that fits: "It is a day to show the importance of giving every child the ___ to feel loved."
questions.explanation: Giving every child the right to feel loved uses the structure of the unit, the right to: a right is something that is owed to every child. Caring and wishing are verb forms that do not name something that is owed, and often is an adverb that tells how many times, not a thing.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) Complete the sentence with the correct form: "Two days ago, Peter gave a lost handbag to the police. Later, the bag owner ___ him a lot for that."
questions.explanation: "Two days ago" and "Later" place the whole story in the past, and thank is a regular verb, so it simply takes -ed. The bare form and the form with -s are present forms, and the form with will looks forward to a day that has not come.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2024) Complete the sentence with the correct form: "Two days ago, Peter saw a handbag under the table in a restaurant. So he ___ it to the police station."
questions.explanation: The story is told in the past ("Two days ago"), and take is irregular: it has its own past form and never takes -ed. The bare form and the form with -s are present forms, and the form with -ed adds the regular ending to a verb that refuses it.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2023) Complete the sentence with the correct form: "Yesterday, my sister ___ many e-mails to our cousins."
questions.explanation: "Yesterday" is over, so the verb goes into the simple past, and write is irregular: it has its own past form and never takes -ed. The bare form and the form with -s are present forms, and the form with -ed adds the regular ending to a verb that refuses it.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025) Complete the sentence with the correct form: "My friends ___ fast food, but I liked the healthy meals my mother cooked."
questions.explanation: "I liked" shows that the whole sentence tells about a time that is over, so the verb goes into the simple past. Prefer is a regular verb, so it takes -ed (its r doubles before the ending): preferred. The bare form and the form with -s are present forms, and the form with will looks to the future.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025) Put these parts in the right order to make a correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The sentence opens with its time word, which carries the capital letter and the comma (Two weeks ago,), then comes the subject (Andy), then the verb in the simple past (prepared), then what he prepared (a surprise party), and last the person it was for, which carries the full stop (for his mother.).

questions.prompt: (Exam 2026) Put the word in brackets in the right tense or form and type it: "Last winter, in the clothes shop, I [find] ___ a nice winter coat and gloves."
questions.explanation: "Last winter" is a finished time, so the verb goes into the simple past. Find is an irregular verb: it takes no -ed and keeps one single past form for every subject, which you have to know by heart.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2025) Put the word in brackets in the right tense or form and type it: "Last year, I decided to follow a healthy lifestyle. I [drink] ___ a lot of water to keep fit."
questions.explanation: "Last year" is a finished time, so the verb goes into the simple past. Drink is an irregular verb: it takes no -ed, and the vowel inside the word is the part that changes.
